title: How Honourable Is the Place
description: How Honourable Is the Place in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 8, headed “The safety and protection of the church, Isa. 26. 1-6”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How hon-ou-ra-ble is the place Where we a-dor-ing stand, Zi-on the glo-ry of the earth, And beau-ty of the land!

lines: Zion the glory of the earth,
The walls of strong salvation made,
Here you shall taste unmingled joys,
You that have known Jehovah's name,
Trust in the Lord, for ever trust,
Strength in the Lord Jehovah dwells,
What tho' the rebels dwell on high,
His arm shall bring them low,
Low' as the caverns of the grave
On Babylon our feet shall tread
The ruins of her walls shall spread

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
